title: Suspicious local scheduled task creation command
description: Detects local Schtasks creation requests whose explicit /tr argument contains a selected user-writable payload or suspicious script/proxy-execution behavior. Standard quoted actions and unquoted executable paths are covered; task names are not payload evidence.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may create a local scheduled task that executes a script, user-writable payload or signed Windows utility for persistence or execution.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE documents scheduled task creation across execution, persistence and privilege escalation. Combining local Schtasks creation with a task action and selected payload behavior is more useful than alerting on every local task, while the separate remote-task rule retains ownership of commands using the documented remote /s option.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify selected suspicious content inside a standard quoted /tr action or unquoted executable argument; leave task-name and executable-launch-path strings out of the payload decision. Complex nested quoting remains outside this heuristic.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Validate the task action, creator and schedule before escalation; software deployment and administrative automation can create local tasks with interpreters or user-space paths.
steps: Confirm the command's result in follow-on process, file, registry or service telemetry; a process-start event records intent and does not prove successful execution.
Review the complete Schtasks command, task name, schedule, /tr action, original filename, parent process, account and endpoint role.
Inspect the referenced payload or remote resource and correlate its file creation, signer, hash, download, child processes and task execution events.
Confirm the task with the responsible deployment or automation owner; otherwise disable it safely, contain the endpoint and investigate the originating process and account.
false_positives: Approved local software deployment, maintenance or administrative automation that creates a task with one of the selected payload forms

validation.expected_outcome: Match selected payload content in /tr; reject task-name/caller-path marker coincidences, remote creation, ordinary managed tasks, queries and unrelated tools.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
